quadrant.why: The horizontal line is zero variance, not a target. Both halves are problems and they are different problems: above it, money is going out faster than the plan allowed; below it, capital is not going into the ground on schedule, which defers the in-service date and therefore the recovery. The vertical line at 50% complete separates the projects where a decision still changes the outcome from the ones where it does not.

nodes.note: NEW, and CORRECTED August 5, 2026 -- it was 'Forecast Snapshot' with three monthly calendarizations, which is not a cadence this customer runs. The version column carries two chains, not one: three plan adoptions (MTP 2024, 2025, 2026), successive within a plan horizon, and three fiscal-year cuts (3+9, 6+6, 9+3), successive within a fiscal year. nodes.label: Plan Vintage
nodes.biz: One issue of a plan or forecast. Members of a chain, ordered by a declared key.
nodes.note: NEW, and CORRECTED August 5, 2026 -- it was 'Forecast Snapshot' with three monthly calendarizations, which is not a cadence this customer runs. The version column carries two chains, not one: three plan adoptions (MTP 2024, 2025, 2026), successive within a plan horizon, and three fiscal-year cuts (3+9, 6+6, 9+3), successive within a fiscal year. Both are `issued` -- nothing approves either -- so neither has an `active` member and a validator applying the approval chain's one-active rule would fail every well-formed row here. The node is what turns 'the plan moved three times' into a coordinate comparison of one measure family instead of three unrelated measures.

items.title: What this excludes
items.text: Projects with no forecast in-service date are excluded, not defaulted to the end of the window — a defaulted date puts value in a month nobody planned it for. Projects already past their forecast date with nothing recorded are listed under the calendar rather than dropped; an empty cell hides exactly the project a reader most needs. Projects already in service carry no filing verdict, because they certified against a date in the past. Projects reaching service after their test-year end are marked later case rather than at risk — that is most of the portfolio, and counting it as exposure is the error that turned three quarters of the list red the first time this ran.
